description: A 2 × 2 composite of mechanical-testing curves for intercritical quenching–annealing (QA) treated low-density δ-TRIP steel plate. All four panels share one y-axis, "True stress (Work hardening rate)/MPa", spanning 0–7000 with ticks every 1000 MPa, and one x-axis, "True strain", spanning 0.0–0.5 with ticks every 0.1. In every panel a red curve is the work hardening rate (WHR) curve and a black curve is the true stress–strain curve; Roman numerals I, II and III, separated by vertical dotted lines, divide each panel into three deformation stages. The panels are (a) QA-620, (b) QA-680, (c) QA-740 and (d) QA-800, each labelled top-right. A yellow circular marker sits on the black curve of every panel; it is annotated "necking point" with an arrow and a short horizontal guide line only in (a). All WHR curves start above 6000 MPa at near-zero strain, fall steeply through stage I, then flatten into a plateau lying just above the 1000 MPa gridline through stages II–III, ending in a near-vertical drop at fracture. Necking/fracture shift to larger strain at higher QA temperature: the necking marker lies left of the 0.3 true-strain tick in (a) and (b), near the 0.4 tick in (d) and between 0.4 and 0.5 in (c). The figure shows that all QA conditions share one three-stage WHR shape, differing mainly in the strain at which necking and failure occur.

subfigures.description: Panel labelled QA-620. Red WHR curve falls steeply from above 6000 MPa near zero strain, a first vertical dotted line at very low strain separates stage I from II, a second dotted line near the 0.3 tick separates II from III; the curve then plateaus just above the 1000 MPa gridline. Yellow necking point with arrow, label "necking point" and a horizontal guide line sits on the black true stress–strain curve, which rises to roughly the 1000–1200 MPa level and then drops near-vertically at fracture.

Panel labelled QA-680. Same construction as (a); the red WHR curve plateaus slightly above the 1000 MPa gridline with the second stage-boundary dotted line closer to the 0.2 tick, and the black curve reaches its yellow necking point at a strain left of the 0.3 tick, followed by an abrupt drop.

Panel labelled QA-740. Red WHR curve decays steeply and plateaus near/below 1100 MPa, with a slight upturn towards the end of stage III; the yellow necking point on the black curve occurs at the largest strain of the four panels, between the 0.4 and 0.5 ticks, with fracture close to the 0.5 tick.

Panel labelled QA-800. Red WHR curve plateaus a little above the 1000 MPa gridline with a small rise before necking; the yellow necking point on the black curve lies near the 0.4 true-strain tick, with a near-vertical drop to zero stress immediately after it.

observations.observation: The figure is a 2 × 2 array of panels, each labelled in its top-right corner: QA-620 (a), QA-680 (b), QA-740 (c) and QA-800 (d).

The shared y-axis is labelled "True stress (Work hardening rate)/MPa" with ticks from 0 to 7000 at 1000 MPa intervals; the shared x-axis is labelled "True strain" with ticks from 0.0 to 0.5 at 0.1 intervals.
Every panel contains one red curve and one black curve, plus the Roman numerals I, II and III separated by vertical dotted lines marking three deformation stages.
The red curves all start above 6000 MPa at near-zero true strain, fall steeply, and then flatten into a plateau lying just above the 1000 MPa gridline.
A yellow circular marker sits on the black true stress–strain curve of every panel; only in (a) is it annotated "necking point" with an arrow and a short horizontal black guide line.
Each black true stress–strain curve terminates in a near-vertical drop to zero stress at fracture, at the smallest true strain in (b) and the largest in (c).
The yellow necking marker lies left of the 0.3 true-strain tick in (a) and (b), near the 0.4 tick in (d), and between the 0.4 and 0.5 ticks in (c).
The caption states that the red lines are work hardening rate curves, the black lines are true stress–strain curves, and the yellow point is the necking point.
The caption calls the specimens "OA specimens", while the panel labels themselves read QA-620/QA-680/QA-740/QA-800 — the caption label does not match the printed panel labels.
The citing text states that the WHR curves of all QA specimens had an analogous shape and could be divided into three stages based on the slopes of the WHR curves.
The citing text attributes stage I to sequential dislocation gliding in ferrite, austenite and tempered martensite according to differences in phase hardness.

The citing text states that after heating at 1050 °C and annealing treatment δ-ferrite grains grew, ferrite grain-boundary density decreased and the dislocation mean free path increased, so the WHR sharply decreased.

The citing text attributes the slowed WHR decline in stage II to grain-boundary and high-density dislocation-tangle hindrance plus the TRIP effect raising WHR, with dislocation gliding, limited dislocation annihilation at grain boundaries and cross slip lowering it.

unreadable_items: No numeric necking or fracture strain/stress values are printed in any panel; all such values can only be read approximately against the 1000 MPa and 0.1 strain gridlines
Caption/graphic label mismatch: caption says "OA specimens", panels are labelled QA-620/680/740/800
